findings.proposedChange: No action. Do NOT dispatch account-store-drift.yml again to 'make it close' — the lookup is `gh issue list --state open`, so a closed issue is invisible to it and a re-dispatch is a no-op that prints 'the audit passed and no tracking issue is open'. findings.claim: (a) account-store-drift.yml reads ONE input — `eval-results:propagation/account/latest.json` plus the `propagation/.bootstrapped` marker, fetched by an anonymous `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch --branch eval-results`. It runs on `cron: '38 6 * * *'` (daily 06:38 UTC) and on `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run` defaulting to **true**. What closes the issue is the `close` policy reaching `gh issue close --reason completed --comment` in the single credentialed step — and that arm is reached only when the decider prints policy=close AND the lookup finds an open issue AND `DRIFT_DRY_RUN` is not the literal string "true".
findings.evidence: /home/user/skills-evals/.github/workflows/account-store-drift.yml: `schedule: - cron: '38 6 * * *'`; `workflow_dispatch.inputs.dry_run.default: true`; step 'Fetch the account audit's published result'; step 'Decide whether the drift issue should exist' invokes `python3 harness/run_account_drift_issue.py evals/propagation --account-latest ../eval-results/propagation/account/latest.json --account-marker ../eval-results/propagation/.bootstrapped`; write step `case "$ISSUE_POLICY" in ... close) ... gh issue close "$number" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --reason completed --comment "$(cat "$BODY_FILE")"`.
findings.proposedChange: Nothing to change. Note for anyone dispatching it later: `dry_run` defaults TRUE, so an unmodified dispatch decides, runs the dedupe lookup, prints the body and exits one line above every write. Clearing the box is what performs the close — which is exactly what run 32580580995 did.

findings.claim: (b) The verdict is a pure function of the published artifact plus a clock. `freshness_verdict(summary, now, max_age_days, bootstrapped)` returns `fresh` only when summary is present, `generated_at` parses, age ≤ `account_audit_max_age_days` (3, from evals/propagation/fixture.yaml) and `status == "pass"`. `decide()` maps reported-failure→open, fresh→close, and stale/missing/unreadable/not-yet-bootstrapped→none. `latest.json` is written by `harness/run_account_audit.py --out`, which reads `~/.claude/skills/synced/manifest.json` on a signed-in surface, and is pushed to the **eval-results** branch by the Tier-3 Routine's bound cloud session — never by a runner. I ran both harness entry points against the live artifact and they return fresh/close.
findings.evidence: Ran in /home/user/skills-evals against a fresh clone of eval-results: `python3 harness/run_propagation.py evals/propagation --gate-only --account-latest .../latest.json --account-marker .../.bootstrapped` → "PASS freshness-gate [fresh]: the account audit passed 0.0 days ago (10 skill(s) checked)", exit 0. `python3 harness/run_account_drift_issue.py evals/propagation --account-latest ... --account-marker ...` → "account-drift-issue [fresh]: policy=close checked=10 skipped=10 drifted=0", exit 0. account_store.py:57 `MANIFEST_RELPATH = Path(".claude")/"skills"/"synced"/"manifest.json"`. eval-results HEAD = 162101b, 2026-08-22 15:02:44 +0000, author `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`, "propagation: account audit badge, byte-identical to the generator [skip ci]"; latest.json = `"status": "pass", "generated_at": "2026-08-22T14:56:28Z", "registry_ref": "b81f6f1b…", "findings": []`; badges/account-store.json = green "10 in sync · 2026-08-22".
findings.proposedChange: No change. Record the mechanism for the next episode: the ONLY thing that moves the verdict is a new `latest.json` on eval-results whose `status` is `pass` and whose `generated_at` is within 3 days. Nothing in either repo's main branch can move it.

findings.claim: (c) CRITICAL QUESTION, ANSWERED — NO, #48 did not have to wait for the Routine, and the same escape hatch exists for the next episode. The artifact that closed it was published at 14:56:28Z, ~9½ hours off the Routine's `0 5 * * *` cron: it came from an on-demand session created per ROUTINE.md's 'Verifying a repair on demand' recipe (`create_session(source_url=…/skills-evals)`), which is a Routine-independent publish path. The reactor's 06:38 schedule is likewise not the only read path — its `workflow_dispatch` with dry_run cleared closes the same minute. So the loop is: human uploads ZIP → an on-demand sourced session republishes latest.json → dispatch account-store-drift.yml with dry_run=false. Both halves were exercised today. Without them the wait is up to ~25½ hours (05:00 publish + 06:38 read).
findings.evidence: latest.json `generated_at` 2026-08-22T14:56:28Z vs Routine cron `0 5 * * *` (list_triggers: next_run_at 2026-08-23T05:04:51Z); the day's Routine publish is the separate 20260822T050747Z.json artifact, which reads `fail`. ROUTINE.md lines 882–960 'Verifying a repair on demand — creating a session for it' spells the `create_session(source_url=…)` recipe and states "`source_url` is the whole trick"; its closing paragraph names the `workflow_dispatch` with dry_run default true as the way to shorten the reactor's clock. Run 32580580995 is that dispatch.
findings.proposedChange: Keep both hatches documented together. ROUTINE.md already carries them; the only thing missing is that today's episode is now the worked example — worth one line in ROUTINE.md recording that the 08-22 repair used exactly this path (upload 14:2xZ → on-demand publish 14:56:28Z → dispatch close 15:04:29Z), so the next reader sees a measured round trip of ~8 minutes rather than a recipe nobody has run.

findings.claim: STEP 2 OF THE RESIDUAL WORK — (f) the pushed agentskills branch is CORRECT, MINIMAL and SAFE to merge, and merging it IS what stops the ZIP workflow re-offering sync-skills. One commit (a691453), one file, one hunk: account-state.json's `sync-skills` entry flips basis observed→asserted, digest ae4a8768…→f2e4328a…, updatedAt→null, plus `asserted_at` and `asserted_from {ref: b81f6f1b…, run_id: 32558665629}`. I verified by effect, not by reading: with the branch's file as state, sync-skills moves from `stale` to `in-sync (asserted)` and `needs_upload` becomes empty. It cannot re-drift the account copy, because it touches no skill payload — account-state.json sits at the repo root precisely so zip_skill() never bundles it.
findings.evidence: `git diff origin/main...origin/record-account-upload/sync-skills-32558665629` → only account-state.json, the hunk above. With MAIN state: `python3 plugins/adam-local/skills/sync-skills/sync_skills.py --account-drift --repos /home/user/agentskills` → `stale sync-skills`. With BRANCH state (`--account-state <branch copy>`): → `in-sync (asserted) sync-skills`, `needs_upload: []`, and the row's registry_digest == recorded_digest == sha256:f2e4328a4317bd5616f8b930ffded49f67e7ee2db81f229ba718273e7be112f7. asserted_from.ref b81f6f1b… == `git rev-parse origin/main` == latest.json's registry_ref, so the assertion is against the tree the artifact was actually built from. PR #118 body: account-state.json "lives at the repo root deliberately — a copy inside a skill directory would be uploaded as part of that skill by zip_skill()".
findings.proposedChange: Open a PR from `record-account-upload/sync-skills-32558665629` into main and merge it with `gh pr merge --merge` (squash is disabled on fleet repos). The PR must be opened by a HUMAN IDENTITY, not by GITHUB_TOKEN — that is why the workflow stops at a branch: `pytest-windows` is required on main and GitHub raises no workflow runs for GITHUB_TOKEN events. agentskills' ci.yml has a bare `pull_request:` with NO paths filter, so an account-state.json-only PR does run all six jobs including pytest-windows; the check will publish. There are currently ZERO open PRs on agentskills. Deadline: before the ZIP workflow's next scheduled run.

findings.claim: STEP 2 IS TIME-BOXED — if the branch is not merged before `cron: '23 6 * * *'` fires (next 2026-08-23 ~06:23 UTC; today's landed 07:05 after cron queueing), the ZIP build re-offers sync-skills and produces a spurious artifact. The published audit will read `fresh` by then, and a fresh verdict contributes nothing AND REMOVES NOTHING from the selection — the union deliberately never lets a passing audit suppress the local recording. So `needs_upload: ['sync-skills']` on unmerged main goes straight through to `names`, count=1.
findings.evidence: account-skill-zips.yml line 68 `- cron: '23 6 * * *'`; lines 82–86 push paths include 'account-state.json'. account_zip_selection.py `audit_drifted()`: "Empty for every status but `reported-failure`, INCLUDING `fresh`"; `select()` stale branch: `names = sorted(set(report["needs_upload"]) | set(contributed))` with the comment "a passing audit contributes nothing and removes nothing". Measured on unmerged main above: needs_upload contains sync-skills.
findings.proposedChange: Merge before ~06:23 UTC on 2026-08-23. The merge is self-verifying: account-state.json is IN the push paths filter, so landing it re-runs account-skill-zips on main, and its job summary should then read `names=[], count=0`. Check that run's summary as the confirmation rather than assuming. Depends on: STEP 2's PR.

findings.claim: TEST RUNNERS — skills-evals has TWO CI commands, in two workflows, and BOTH files really run their tests (the opposite of agentskills' scripts/ trap): each ends in a `unittest.main()` call, so invoking the file directly is a genuine gate here. ci.yml runs `python3 test/run_tests.py`; propagation.yml's `gate` job runs `python3 test/test_propagation.py` with `AGENTSKILLS_DIR` set to a side-by-side agentskills checkout. I ran both against the current tree.
findings.evidence: /home/user/skills-evals/.github/workflows/ci.yml:69 `run: python3 test/run_tests.py`. /home/user/skills-evals/.github/workflows/propagation.yml:154 `run: python3 test/test_propagation.py` under `env: AGENTSKILLS_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/agentskills`. run_tests.py:1073 `unittest.main()`; test_propagation.py ends `unittest.main(verbosity=1)`. Use `python3 test/run_tests.py` for the eval harness. Report the test COUNT alongside the exit code, as above. Note this is NOT the agentskills command: over there the only real runner is `python3 -m pytest scripts/ plugins/*/skills/*/tests/ plugins/*/skills/*/scripts/ -q`, and running a scripts/test_*.py file directly exits 0 having asserted nothing.
